html:
Obock is a small port on the north shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura, bought by France from local Afar rulers in 1862, the first step toward the colony that became Djibouti.

France wanted a base on the route to the Indian Ocean, and the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 made one more valuable. When Britain refused French ships coal at Aden during a war with China in the 1880s, France built up Obock as a coaling station.

Its harbour was poor, and in the 1890s the capital moved across the gulf to Djibouti. Obock stayed a small town, but its purchase set the frame of a territory shared by Afar in the north and Somali Issa in the south, a divide that shaped the civil war.
sum: Obock is a small port on the north shore of the Gulf of Tadjoura, bought by France from local Afar rulers in 1862, the first step toward the colony that became Djibouti.
